Choosing the best health insurance in India 2025 can feel overwhelming, especially with so many plans, features, and confusing terms. In this in-depth video, I bring you a clear and honest Star Health Insurance review, covering everything you must know before buying a policy. Whether you're comparing Star Health with other insurers or specifically researching the Super Star plan, this video will help you make an informed decision.

We start with Star Health’s core performance metrics — Claim Settlement Ratio (CSR), Incurred Claim Ratio (ICR), and complaint volume. These numbers reveal how reliable an insurer truly is, and understanding them is crucial before choosing a long-term health insurance partner. I break them down in a simple, practical way so you’ll know exactly how Star Health is performing in 2025.

Then we dive deep into the Star Super Star variant. This is one of Star Health’s most popular plans, and I explain all the important features including room rent limits, pre- and post-hospitalisation coverage, OPD features, sub-limits, waiting periods, and unique add-ons. One of the most talked-about benefits — Freeze Your Age — is also explained clearly so you understand when it is useful, when it is not, and who actually needs it.

Along with Super Star, I also review other key Star Health policies such as Star Comprehensive and Health Assure. This helps you compare the plans side-by-side and understand which one suits salaried individuals, families, senior citizens, and people looking for high cover at affordable premiums.

To make things even more helpful, this video includes an exclusive comparison of HDFC Ergo Secure vs Star Health Super Star. If you’re confused between these two insurers, this segment will give you complete clarity on coverage, pricing, claims experience, and long-term benefits.

If you're searching for best health insurance plans, Star Health review, Freeze Your Age explained, or HDFC Ergo vs Star Health, this video will answer all your questions. Watch till the end for my final recommendation on who should consider Star Health and who should explore other insurers.

comments.text:
Many people believe that a high CSR (Claim Settlement Ratio) means all claims are passed or fully paid.
That belief is factually wrong.

Let’s understand how CSR actually works.

CSR = Number of claims settled ÷ Number of claims reported

The key word here is “settled” — not “approved”.

In insurance reporting, a claim is considered settled the moment it is CLOSED, regardless of the outcome.

That means a claim is counted as “settled” even if:
	•	It is fully approved
	•	It is partially paid with heavy deductions
	•	It is 100% rejected

Yes — even a fully rejected claim improves CSR once the insurer issues a final decision.
